events.headline: Puka Nacua catches 17 of 24 targets for 138 yards and a TD as Bills beat the Rams 37-34 in OT; James Cook scores twice but fumbles twice
events.detail: Nacua set a Monday Night Football record for catches on a career-high 24 targets as Matthew Stafford went 40-of-54 for 383 yards and three TDs; Davante Adams caught two touchdowns and Tyler Higbee added 5-83. Kyren Williams tied it with a 1-yard TD run in the final seconds of regulation. For Buffalo, Cook ran 25 times for 111 yards and two TDs (per PFT) but fumbled twice, the second one recovered by the Rams in overtime. Josh Allen threw only 19 passes and ran 10 times for 121 yards and a touchdown.
events.so_what: A 24-target night confirms Nacua as the most bankable weekly volume in the Rams offense, with Adams the red-zone finisher beside him: both are every-week starters. Cook's 25 carries and goal-line work are the RB1 profile, but two fumbles in one game is a real cost here at -2 per lost fumble, and a ball-security benching is the one way his touches shrink. Allen's 121 rushing yards and a TD are exactly the konami rushing value this scoring pays for, which keeps him a top QB start even on a 19-attempt night.

source.label: NBC Sports PFT: Bills beat Rams 37-34 in overtime in instant classic

events.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) limited on Seattle's estimated report for Thursday at Denver; Zach Charbonnet (knee) not expected to make his debut
events.detail: Seattle did not practice Monday, so the first Week 6 report was an estimate. Smith-Njigba hurt the ankle in the 32-29 loss to San Francisco, where he went 5-102-1, and was listed limited; local reporting expects him to play. Mike Macdonald said Charbonnet will likely not play Thursday ('as of right now, the answer is no, subject to change') because the short week leaves no on-field practice time. He is still on PUP, and his 21-day window closes next week, so he must be activated before Week 7 to play this season. George Holani (ribs/knee) and backup QB Drew Lock (forearm) were also limited.
events.so_what: Smith-Njigba is still a start for Thursday unless the Wednesday report turns into a DNP; check before the early lock, since Thursday games strand anyone you forget. Charbonnet stays a bench stash for at least one more week, and the activation deadline next week is the date that tells you whether he is worth the roster spot on a 5-man bench.

source.label: Spokesman-Review: Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet likely won’t be back for Broncos game

events.headline: David Montgomery (groin) week to week, per DeMeco Ryans; Woody Marks leads the Texans backfield
events.detail: Montgomery left Sunday's win over Tennessee in the second quarter with 11 yards on five carries. On Monday DeMeco Ryans called him week to week. Woody Marks had 49 yards on 12 carries and three catches for 21 through three quarters; Dare Ogunbowale is the only other active back. Houston also added Marvin Harrison Jr. by trade this weekend.
events.so_what: Week to week means plan on Marks as the lead back for at least Week 6, which makes him a FLEX start and the priority add in this backfield. Montgomery is an IR-slot candidate only if the team moves him there; otherwise he is a bench hold, not a drop.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: Will Shipley (foot) has a partial plantar fascia tear; Sirianni hopeful Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith return for Week 6
events.detail: Shipley started with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) out and Tank Bigsby on IR, scored his first career TD and left in the first half of the 19-17 London loss to Jacksonville. Adam Schefter reported Monday it is a partial plantar fascia tear that could cost multiple weeks. Dameon Pierce finished with 14 yards on 11 carries. Nick Sirianni said Monday he is hopeful Barkley returns for Week 6 against Carolina, and the same for DeVonta Smith, who has missed two games with a hamstring.
events.so_what: Shipley is a multi-week stash at best now; drop him before anyone with a role. "Hopeful" is a forecast, so hold Barkley and Smith and read Wednesday through Friday practice reports before starting either. If Barkley sits again, nobody left in this backfield is a reliable FLEX.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) ruled out vs. Browns; Browns WR KC Concepcion also out after a helmet-to-helmet hit
events.detail: The Jets rookie TE was ruled out early in the fourth quarter after a hit that forced a fumble; he had two catches for three yards. It is his first documented concussion and he is in the protocol, and Aaron Glenn said Monday he remains in the protocol ahead of New England.  Mason Taylor and Jeremy Ruckert absorb the TE snaps. On the other side, Cleveland's KC Concepcion left in the first half after a helmet-to-helmet hit and was ruled out (AP, via KSAT, Oct. 11).
events.so_what: Sadiq was not producing before the hit, so plan around him for Week 6; Mason Taylor is the beneficiary and a streaming TE option if Sadiq sits. Concepcion is a protocol wait before he is startable again.

source.label: CBS Sports: Jets' Kenyon Sadiq, concussion confirmed

events.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) sits as Tyler Huntley rallies Ravens past Falcons in OT; Jackson has a "real chance" to return vs. Cleveland
events.detail: Jackson watched from the sideline in street clothes. Huntley went 24 of 32 for 201 yards and two TDs, ran six times for 20 yards, threw the tying score to Devontez Walker with 40 seconds left and won it on a 1-yard sneak in overtime. Derrick Henry ran for 102 yards against the league's top-ranked run defense and took the direct snap on the tying two-point try. Ian Rapoport reported Jackson has a "real chance" to return next week against Cleveland, pending how the ankle responds to rehab; nothing official yet. On Monday Jesse Minter said it is not clear whether Jackson will practice Wednesday.
events.so_what: A return is a forecast, not a clearance, and his coach would not commit to Wednesday practice, so keep a QB2 rostered through Friday's report. Huntley's line (two passing TDs, a rushing TD, short yardage) is the streaming ceiling in this format and only matters if Jackson sits again. Henry's volume held without Jackson, so he stays a locked RB start either way.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: Michael Penix Jr. (ribs): no update Monday, Falcons will know more Wednesday; Schefter says not considered serious
events.detail: Penix was hurt on a fourth-quarter sack by Tavius Robinson and walked off under his own power after going 19 of 32 for 240 yards and a TD to Kyle Pitts. Tua Tagovailoa took over and threw the game-ending interception in overtime on a pass meant for Drake London. Penix said the injury is not a long-term issue; Kevin Stefanski said the team will know more once imaging is done. Drake London had 7 catches for 118 yards on 11 targets and has averaged 20.6 fantasy points in the three games Penix has started. On Monday Kevin Stefanski had no update, saying the team will have a better understanding Wednesday; Adam Schefter reported the injury is not considered serious and Atlanta will evaluate him before deciding on Week 6 against Chicago.
events.so_what: Hold Penix but do not plan around him; a rib injury on a pocket passer is a pain-tolerance call that can drift to Sunday, so line up a QB2 if he is your starter. London's production has tracked Penix, so a Tagovailoa start is a downgrade in volume quality rather than a bench call: he stays a WR start either way.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will "miss some time," per Shanahan; Christian Kirk (calf) not expected back in Week 6
events.detail: Samuel was favoring his right hamstring earlier in the game, then lost a fumble on a carry and stayed down; he left with 5:06 left in the third quarter and was ruled out. Receiver Jacob Cowing hurt an ankle on a kick return a few plays later. Mike Evans, playing through a rib injury for a second week, caught 7 of 10 targets for 113 yards and a TD. San Francisco plays Monday night at Washington next week. On Monday Kyle Shanahan said Samuel will miss some time and that Christian Kirk (calf), banged up again Sunday, is not expected back in Week 6.
events.so_what: Samuel is out for a stretch: move him to an IR slot if the team lists him there, otherwise bench him and pick up a WR or FLEX replacement. With Samuel and Kirk both out, Evans (already near a 37% target share) is the clear first read and an every-week WR start.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: Steelers WR room thins: Michael Pittman Jr. on IR, Roman Wilson (finger) out multiple weeks
events.detail: Pittsburgh moved Pittman to injured reserve Saturday after he aggravated his left foot (plantar fasciitis, which already cost him Week 2); he is out at least four games. Roman Wilson then left Sunday's win over the Colts with a finger injury and is expected to miss multiple weeks, per Jeremy Fowler, and Mike McCarthy ruled out Wilson and Ben Skowronek (calf) for Week 6 against Tampa Bay. Rookie Germie Bernard is the next man up.
events.so_what: Pittman goes in an IR slot rather than eating one of the 5 bench spots. With Wilson also out, Bernard inherits a near full-time role, which makes him the speculative add, though a thin Steelers passing game caps his weekly ceiling.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) day-to-day after leaving in a walking boot
events.detail: Judkins hurt his ankle in the 17-12 loss to the Jets and was seen in a walking boot after the game. Todd Monken said Monday he is considered day-to-day and could play in Week 6 against Baltimore; Wednesday practice is the first real read. He had 14 carries for 44 yards and is averaging three yards a carry this season.
events.so_what: Day-to-day is a designation, not a clearance, and the boot plus a three-yard average make him a shaky start even if he plays. Hold him through Friday's report and have a FLEX fallback ready.

source.label: NBC Sports (PFT): Quinshon Judkins day-to-day with ankle injury

events.headline: A.J. Brown (high ankle) may return to practice this week, per Vrabel; still on IR
events.detail: Brown has been on injured reserve since a Week 1 high ankle sprain. Mike Vrabel said Monday he may return to practice this week, adding that when he will be back "remains to be seen." New England beat the Raiders 45-17 Sunday.
events.so_what: A practice return opens his 21-day window but is not activation, so he stays in an IR slot until the Patriots move him to the active roster. If he is on your wire in a deep league, this is the week to stash him before he is activated.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) not expected to practice this week
events.detail: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Monday that Tyson, dealing with a hamstring injury, is not expected to return to practice this week.
events.so_what: No practice this week points to a missed Week 6; bench him or move on if you are short on bench space, since hamstrings tend to linger.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Monday Oct. 12

events.headline: D.J. Moore (shoulder) sits out Monday night; Bills beat the Rams 37-34 in OT without him
events.detail: Moore, Questionable after one limited practice on the re-aggravated left shoulder, did not play at SoFi. Keon Coleman caught Josh Allen's only touchdown pass, and Khalil Shakir broke a 57-yard catch-and-run in overtime. Allen threw only 19 passes (12-210-1-1) and ran for 121 yards and a score, so the Bills' passing volume was thin with Moore and Joshua Palmer both out. No new timeline for Moore was given in the recap.
events.so_what: Two straight weeks of the same shoulder costing Moore playing time makes him a week-to-week lineup gamble rather than a locked WR2: wait for Friday's designation before starting him in Week 6. A 19-attempt game plan caps every Bills receiver while Allen is carrying the offense with his legs (the konami rushing value is where Buffalo's points are landing), so Coleman is a TD-dependent FLEX, not a volume play.

source.label: ESPN: Bills 37-34 Rams (Oct 12, 2026) game recap

events.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (right ankle) ruled out vs. Raiders and could miss significant time; Rhamondre Stevenson takes over
events.detail: Henderson was hurt on a sideline tackle in the second quarter, needed help to the locker room, and was ruled out early in the third, finishing with 22 rushing yards on four carries plus a 16-yard catch. It is the same ankle-area history that cost him the opener. Stevenson ran 13 times for 64 yards and a TD with three catches for 21 in a 45-17 win; Corey Kiner added 52 yards on six carries, much of it in garbage time. No diagnosis or timetable yet. The Jets are next.
events.so_what: Stevenson becomes a lead back on an offense scoring at will, which makes him a starting RB or FLEX next week while Henderson sits. Henderson goes on hold rather than the bench-or-drop pile until a diagnosis lands. Kiner is the handcuff dart if the absence is long.

source.label: NBC Sports: Henderson (ankle) ruled out vs. Raiders

events.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) ruled out in the opening minute at New Orleans; Aaron Jones (knee) exits, returns and runs for 113
events.detail: Hockenson's head hit the turf on a 7-yard catch 38 seconds into the game and he was ruled out. He must clear the concussion protocol, and Minnesota has its Week 6 bye next, which buys him time. Aaron Jones left late in the first quarter with a knee injury after losing a fumble at the Saints' 7, returned about 20 minutes later, and finished with 113 yards on 25 carries and the go-ahead fourth-quarter TD. Gavin Bartholomew played as the TE1. The Vikings won 23-13 to go 5-0.
events.so_what: The bye means Hockenson costs nothing extra this week; he should be on track for Week 7 if he clears protocol, so hold him. Jones carried 25 times after the knee scare, which says the injury is minor, but check the post-bye report before trusting it. Bartholomew is not a pickup with the starter likely back after the bye.

source.label: ESPN: Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson suffers concussion against Saints

events.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) active at New Orleans after a Questionable tag
events.detail: Jefferson is on the Vikings' active list for the 1:00 ET game at New Orleans after three limited practices with the ankle sprain. His workload is not confirmed. Jordan Addison is inactive (separate item) and Odell Beckham Jr., elevated Saturday, is also inactive, so the receiver depth behind him is thin.
events.so_what: Start Jefferson as a WR1. With Addison and Beckham both out he is the only established receiver, so the target share should hold even if the ankle trims his snaps. Minnesota is on bye in Week 6.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 5 inactives and injury tracker, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive at New Orleans
events.detail: Addison was downgraded to Doubtful Sunday morning and is on the inactive list. Odell Beckham Jr., elevated from the practice squad Saturday as cover, is inactive too. Justin Jefferson is active.
events.so_what: Bench Addison now; he scores zero. Jefferson absorbs the extra targets and is a locked start. The Vikings bye in Week 6 means Addison is a two-week hole, so plan the Week 6 replacement now.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 5 inactives and injury tracker, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) active at New England despite a Friday DNP
events.detail: Jeanty is not on the Raiders' inactive list (WR Jalen Nailor, QB Aidan O'Connell, S Tristin McCollum, RB Roman Hemby, S Dalton Johnson, G Trey Zuhn III, DT JJ Pegues). He went full, limited, then DNP last week; whether he carries a reduced workload is not reported.
events.so_what: Start him as your RB. The full-limited-DNP trend is the risk: Mike Washington Jr. is the handcuff and steals more work if the foot flares mid-game, so do not chase Washington as a start.

source.label: Raiders.com: Week 5 inactives vs. New England Patriots

events.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) active vs. Giants; Stefon Diggs inactive
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 9 item. McLaurin, Questionable after missing Wednesday and Thursday practice and returning limited Friday, is on the active list for Sunday. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported beforehand that he was likely not a full go. Diggs (hamstring) and Marcus Mariota (knee) are inactive; Jayden Daniels returns from his elbow injury. Steady rain was falling in Washington before kickoff.
events.so_what: McLaurin plays, but a limited snap count on a re-tweak-prone hamstring in a rain game caps him as a FLEX. Diggs scores zero. Rain trims the passing ceiling for Daniels, but his rushing floor keeps him a start. Watch whether the hamstring holds through the week before trusting McLaurin as a WR2 again.

source.label: Hogs Haven: Commanders vs. Giants inactives, Terry McLaurin will play

events.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) misses a third straight game; Tyson Bagent benched in a 31-7 loss at Green Bay
events.detail: Williams (Grade 2 hamstring strain, Sept. 20) was inactive. Bagent started, went 12-of-21 for 87 yards and two interceptions, and was benched early in the fourth quarter for Case Keenum. Ben Johnson has called Williams week-to-week and would not commit to a return date after the game. Williams practiced on a limited basis this week; Atlanta is next.
events.so_what: Keep Williams benched until he logs a full practice week; a hamstring that has already cost three games is a re-injury risk, and the konami rushing that makes him valuable is exactly what it limits. Bagent is not a start anywhere. Chicago's fantasy output runs through D'Andre Swift until Williams returns.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Packers dominate banged-up Bears as Tyson Bagent is benched late

events.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) not expected to play vs. Denver; Quentin Johnston out
events.detail: ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning that McConkey is not expected to play after not practicing all week. The Chargers play the 4:25 ET window, so the official inactive list is not out yet. Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quad) are already out, leaving Tre' Harris and Oronde Gadsden as Justin Herbert's top targets against a Broncos secondary missing both starting outside corners.
events.so_what: Take McConkey out of your lineup now rather than waiting on a late-window inactive list. Tre' Harris is a FLEX-grade play as the de facto WR1, and Gadsden gains targets too.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Week 5 NFL live updates, Oct. 11, 2026

events.headline: Texans complete trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.; Cardinals get 2027 second- and sixth-round picks
events.detail: Houston sent 2027 second- and sixth-round picks to Arizona for Harrison and a 2027 seventh, per ESPN and NFL Network. He was inactive Sunday while the deal was finalized and reunites with C.J. Stroud, his Ohio State quarterback in 2021-22. Harrison had 5 catches on 12 targets for 85 yards and a TD through four games. In Arizona, Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne and Jeremiyah Love all had more targets than him. Houston (now 1-4) also lost David Montgomery to a groin injury Sunday.
events.so_what: Houston needed a second receiver behind Nico Collins, so Harrison lands in a role with real targets to win rather than a crowded room; treat him as a FLEX with WR2 upside once he has a practice week with Stroud, not a Week 6 auto-start. In Arizona his departure consolidates looks for McBride and Wilson. Do not sell Harrison at his Arizona price.

source.label: ESPN: Texans complete trade with Cardinals for WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) active and cleared, scores in 31-24 win at Miami
events.detail: Chase cleared the concussion protocol after a Questionable tag and caught 6 passes for 77 yards and a TD. Joe Burrow threw four TDs on 23-of-31 passing for 190 yards, spreading them to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, Tanner Hudson and Chase. Tee Higgins (groin/neck) was also Questionable; his game status is not confirmed in the coverage found.
events.so_what: Chase is out of the protocol and back to an every-week WR1 start. Burrow's four-TD game is worth more at 4 points a TD than raw yardage suggests, but 190 yards is a thin base, so treat him as a solid QB start, not a breakout.

source.label: NBC Sports: Joe Burrow's four touchdown passes lead Bengals over Dolphins

events.headline: Jaylen Warren piles up 188 scrimmage yards and two long TDs as the Steelers beat the Colts
events.detail: Warren ran 15 times for 101 yards and a 50-yard TD and caught 6 passes for 87 yards, including an 80-yard catch-and-run, in a 34-22 win. ESPN notes he has played nearly every snap for three weeks while Rico Dowdle (toe) was out, even though Mike McCarthy has said he wants a two-back system. Aaron Rodgers threw for 235 yards and three TDs. Jonathan Taylor ran 15 times for 45 yards for Indianapolis.
events.so_what: Warren is a locked RB start while he owns the snaps, but this line rested on two 50-plus-yard plays, and Dowdle's return is the stated threat to the share. Keep starting him; do not sell the week as a new floor. Dowdle is a stash only while he is still out.

source.label: NBC Sports: Jaylen Warren runs over Colts as Steelers win 34-22

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love stuffed on 5 of 12 carries in a 45-21 loss to Detroit; Tyler Allgeier challenging for work
events.detail: ESPN's Week 5 takeaways credit Love with 2.2 fantasy points, minus-21 rushing yards over expected, and stuffs on five of 12 carries, and say Tyler Allgeier is challenging for carries in the Arizona backfield.
events.so_what: Love drops from a locked RB start to a FLEX on a team that trailed by three scores, and a committee would cut his weekly floor further. Allgeier is a worthwhile add for anyone short at RB if the split shows up again next week.

source.label: ESPN: Big questions, lessons from NFL Week 5
